approach: Derive the limit in code at dispatch and store it on the job record. `AcceptedReading::allowed_paths()` (briefs.rs) returns the reading's deliverable paths when a criterion has a limiting phrase, and `None` otherwise. The Job gets an optional `allowed_paths` field, set where the Job is built in run/mod.rs. A path-only helper `outside_allowed_paths(allowed, changed)` sits beside `unchanged_planned_files`, with the same `normal_path` normalisation. It runs at two points. (1) After every producer report in `producer_loop` (run/producer.rs, where the loop actually lives): an outside file joins the one send-back through a new `send_back_text_scoped`, which names each path and says to revert it. If the diff is still outside after the shared send-back, it gets one extra scope-only send-back. (2) At the head of `check_and_verify`, before the decision gate, CI push and verifier: it re-reads the candidate's changes. A still-outside diff, or a resumed candidate that never went through the loop, closes the job as Failed. The reason starts with `SCOPE_REASON_PREFIX` and names the paths, and `retry_findings` carries that reason to a retry's producer. A job with no stored list is never checked. Only Rust and CHANGELOG.md change; no prompt, governance file or records/ file.

decisions.choice: Derive the allowed list from the accepted reading in code, in `AcceptedReading::allowed_paths(&self) -> Option<Vec<String>>` (briefs.rs). It returns the deliverable paths, with a leading `./` removed and duplicates dropped, when some criterion matches `limits_changed_files(text)`. It returns `None` when no criterion matches or when the reading has no deliverables.
decisions.reason: The reading says the limit is derived in code from the accepted criteria and deliverables, and the reader prompt has no token headroom. A method on the existing view needs no new field on `AcceptedReading`, so none of its struct literals change (send_back.rs:214, reading.rs:5922, run_pin_tests.rs:1047). An empty list is never stored, because it would flag every file.

rejected.option: Add an allowed_paths output field to the reader or to Reading
rejected.why: Out of scope: no new reader output field, and prompts are not edited.

rejected.option: Use the plan's files plus the deliverables (as `planned_paths` does)
rejected.why: The limit is the accepted reading's, not the planner's; plan files can be broader than what the user accepted.

rejected.option: Treat any criterion containing 'only' as limiting
rejected.why: Too many false positives ('only the new test fails without the fix'). The matcher uses a fixed phrase list.

decisions.choice: `limits_changed_files(text)` is a pure phrase matcher. It lowercases the text and compares words with every non-alphanumeric run turned into one space. It matches these contiguous phrases: `no file outside`, `no files outside`, `no other file(s)`, `nothing outside`, `production unchanged`, `production code unchanged`, `production code is unchanged`, `production is unchanged`. It also matches the literal `test-only` or `tests-only`, and `test only change|diff|job`. Last, it matches the word `only` followed later by `may change`, `may be changed`, `is changed` or `are changed`.
decisions.reason: It covers the request's examples ('no file outside X changed', 'test-only, production unchanged') and the reading's 'only ... may change' form while leaving this job's own criteria unmatched. The producer for this job edits producer.rs and store.rs, which are not in its deliverable list, so a false match would flag them.

rejected.option: A model call or reader-supplied flag to judge limiting criteria
rejected.why: Not a code check, and it needs a new reader field or prompt change.

decisions.choice: Store the list on the Job record as `allowed_paths: Option<Vec<String>>` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, set in the `Job` literal at run/mod.rs:994. Read it back in the run through `ctx.job.job`, which is set at run/mod.rs:1053.
decisions.reason: This is how `pin` and `dispatch_branch` were added, so older records still parse under `deny_unknown_fields`. The same stored list serves a fresh run, a retry and a resumed candidate, because `resume_candidate` (run/mod.rs ~650) uses the same `ctx`.

rejected.option: Recompute the list from `accepted` at each check
rejected.why: The request says to store it with the job, and the stored value is what is auditable.

decisions.choice: Check at two points. (1) `producer_loop` (run/producer.rs ~268-366): compute the changed list once from `snapshot.change_list()`, call `outside_allowed_paths`, and add the result to the break condition and to `problems`. It is not added to `report_problems`, because the job ends before the verifier. (2) The head of `check_and_verify` (run/mod.rs ~1565): if `recorded_checks.is_none()` and a list is stored, compare `closing.candidate.changes` with it. On a hit, call `self.failure` with a reason starting `SCOPE_REASON_PREFIX` that names each path, keep `changed_paths` as the decision branch does, and return before the CI push, the early PR and the verifier.
decisions.reason: The brief asks for the check at hand-off and again before verification. Point 2 is what stops a diff that is still outside after the loop's send-backs, and a resumed candidate that never went through the loop. It follows the pattern the decision gate already uses.

rejected.option: Check only in the producer loop
rejected.why: A diff still outside after the last send-back would reach the verifier, and a resumed candidate would skip the check.
The producer's working directory is already gone there, so the producer could not be sent back to fix it.

decisions.choice: Give an out-of-scope diff its own extra send-back, constant `SCOPE_SEND_BACKS = 1`, counted apart from `send_backs` (`PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` stays 1). The loop's limit test becomes `send_backs >= PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS && !(outside non-empty && scope_send_backs < SCOPE_SEND_BACKS)`. At most 3 producer runs happen, and only for a job with a stored list.
decisions.reason: Criterion 4 asks that an out-of-list change made after the first send-back is sent back again before the verifier. The shared limit of 1 would make that impossible. Reverting a file is cheap, and a job with no list is unchanged.

rejected.option: Raise PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS to 2 for all jobs
rejected.why: It would change unrelated behavior and the existing tests that pin one send-back (run_pin_tests.rs:1336).

rejected.option: Loop until the diff is clean
rejected.why: Unbounded producer cost; the second check bounds it.

decisions.choice: Add `send_back_text_scoped(brief, unmet, unchanged, replay, gate, outside)` in send_back.rs. `send_back_text_full` delegates to it with `&[]`. The sentence says to restore each file to the base content, or delete it if it was added, and that a file still outside afterwards closes the job before the verifier runs. With an empty `outside` the text is byte-for-byte what `send_back_text_full` gives today.
decisions.reason: The signatures and expected text pinned by the existing tests (send_back.rs ~363-412, run_pin_tests.rs ~1133-1287) stay unchanged.

decisions.reason: A job closed at point 2 has no verification, so without this the retry's producer would not be told which files to leave alone.

risks.risk: A phrase match on an innocent criterion stores a list and blocks a legitimate diff, such as the files this very job must change (producer.rs, store.rs) beyond the 8 listed deliverables.

risks.mitigation: The new field is optional, skipped when None and defaulted when absent. Existing records parse (new test). It is written only for a limited job.

risks.risk: Changing the loop's send-back limit and break condition alters behavior for jobs with no stored list.

risks.risk: The fake reader's gate may refuse the extra criterion that the end-to-end tests add.
risks.mitigation: The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-core scope_send_back` and adjusts the wrapper only. If the reader's gate refuses the extra criterion, the producer reports it rather than changing the gate.
